thread:
incident-bot: Paging @eng-oncall: Canary deploy for release v3.14 in prod/us-west-2 failing health checks (error: KMS decrypt denied). Impacting ~10-15% of inference requests in the canary cohort. Please acknowledge and triage. :rotating_light:

alex (eng-oncall): acked. I'm on it. pulling logs now.

maria (eng-sre): I see repeated `PermissionDenied` from kms:Decrypt in the ingress logs: `AccessDeniedException: User: role/redwood-service is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:...` Looks like the key got rotated or grants were dropped during the deploy.

samir (deploy): canary image reads encrypted model_keys from SSM/EncryptedParam. This was a config-only rollout (env var update for KMS key alias). I pushed `KMS_ALIAS=alias/redwood/v3` earlier.

alex (eng-oncall): timeline? which deploy ID?

deploy-bot: deploy v3.14 started by @samir at 1763001000, canary 10% to prod/us-west-2, config change: KMS_ALIAS -> alias/redwood/v3

maria (eng-sre): reproduce locally: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://enc --key-id alias/redwood/v3` returns AccessDenied for the role used by the service. The previous alias `alias/redwood/v2` still works for the same role.

lee (support): Customer impact: support queue showing increased errors for customers on us-west-2 — a handful of enterprise tenants reporting 403s when calling /v1/infer. Ticket IDs attached in support system.

alex (eng-oncall): ok immediate plan: 1) kill new feature flag using canary kill to stop routing traffic to canary 2) if kill fails, rollback the deployment 3) investigate KMS grant/rotation with security. Who can toggle the flag?

samir (deploy): I can flip the canary route. Doing `curl -X POST https://console.internal/flags/toggle -d 'flag=use_kms_v3&state=off' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'` now.

samir (deploy): toggled `use_kms_v3` -> OFF :white_check_mark: 

ops-bot: routing updated: canary traffic to v3.14 removed, backfilling to stable v3.13 in us-west-2.

maria (eng-sre): metrics: error rate in canary cohort dropped immediately from 12% to baseline <1% after flag toggle. Good. But some in-flight requests may still see errors.

alex (eng-oncall): still seeing 502 spikes in cloudfront logs around 1763001380. Are those from live in-flight canary?

maria (eng-sre): yes likely. Recommend rolling back the replica set to v3.13 to be safe. I'll coordinate rollback if samir gives the go-ahead.

samir (deploy): initiating rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-api -n prod --to-revision=42`

deploy-bot: rollback started for redwood-api in prod/us-west-2 at 1763001505 by @samir.

maria (eng-sre): watching pods come up. healthchecks green on new pods.

lee (support): updating affected customers: telling them we detected a canary config error related to key rotation and have removed canary traffic; full rollback in progress. ETA 10-15m.

alex (eng-oncall): paging rotation/keys team for permanent fix: @security @infra. Maria, can you capture exact IAM denial and policy delta?

maria (eng-sre): capturing diffs: noticed that when the alias was created it was attached to a multi-tenant key where `kms:Decrypt` grants are explicit via key policy. The service role had an explicit grant to alias/redwood/v2 but not to v3. Looks like alias creation step didn't propagate grants. I have the key-id: `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01`.

ops-bot: rollback completed at 1763001789. All pods on v3.13.

maria (eng-sre): post-rollback metrics: error rate back to <1% for all regions. No customer-facing 5xxs observed after rollback complete.

samir (deploy): summary of immediate remediation: 1) toggled feature flag to stop canary 2) rolled back deployment to v3.13 3) opened PR to revert KMS_ALIAS change in config for the stable branch.

alex (eng-oncall): severity? Customer impact was limited to canary cohort but some customers saw errors — I'd call this a SEV2 (partial degradation affecting subset of customers).

lee (support): affected customers list: 7 enterprise tenants, 23 dev/team orgs; all contacted with incident notice and workaround (retries/rollback).

maria (eng-sre): next steps for permanent fix: - Confirm key grants for alias/redwood/v3 and update key policy or create explicit grants for role/redwood-service - Add automated integration test that attempts `kms:Decrypt` with service role during canary rollout (pre-traffic check) - Add gating to deploy pipeline: if new KMS_ALIAS present, run key-permission sanity check as part of canary acceptance.

samir (deploy): I will revert the config change and add a pipeline check (I'll open a ticket and assign).

alex (eng-oncall): handing off to maria for follow-up postmortem and to own the follow-up action items. I'll stay available for escalation.

maria (eng-sre): acknowledged. I'll schedule a brief postmortem, include timeline, root cause (missing kms:Decrypt grant on new alias), and the remediation plan.

lee (support): I'll prepare a customer-facing summary for the affected tenants.

incident-bot: Incident annotated as SEV2, incident id INC-2026-1763001122. Postmortem due in 72 hours.

alex (eng-oncall): closing chat for live mitigation. If anything regresses re-open. Nice work team. :thumbsup: 

maria (eng-sre): postmortem notes (to be transferred to doc): "During a canary-only config rollout we introduced a new KMS alias without updating key grants. Canary pods started using alias v3 and failed `kms:Decrypt` resulting in 4xx/5xx errors for the canary cohort. Immediate mitigation: toggle feature flag to stop routing to canary, rollback to the previous stable release. Follow-ups: pipeline gating, key-grant automation, and monitoring alert for KMS permission anomalies."

samir (deploy): filed ticket: RDW-3456 "KMS alias deploy check and revert for v3 rollout" assigned to samir, due in 5 days.

lee (support): ticket to customers created: CS-7892.

alex (eng-oncall): last check: dashboards stable. I'll close the incident channel in 30m if no new errors. Thanks all.
